Contract says jobs from the API have to come out in the same order they did before, that's non-negotiable per legal. And separately the privacy office wants full traceability on every job execution, who touched what data and when, timestamps that hold up later. Trying to figure out how to redo the queue without blowing up either one.

two things are nagging at me though. devops capped us at 512mb memory and 64 threads max for this service, so the per-request spawn thing has to go at some point. but also our prod clients have been calling this exact function, same signature, same blocking behavior, for like three years now. any change there breaks people.

Right now the export is a single synchronous call from the app server, and if more than a couple analysts hit it at once we're going to choke the box. I want to move this to a queue with workers that can safely retry without duplicating output, so we're not rearchitecting this again in six months when the whole research org wants to run exports at the same time. Separately there's also the 2.1 spec stuff about field names and column order that some scripts rely on, but that feels like a smaller detail compared to the scaling issue.

Every time we get a burst of concurrent uploads, worker nodes start throwing OOM errors and it cascades across the cluster because the queue just backs up. I keep pushing for a rewrite that streams the transforms instead of materializing the whole thing. Meanwhile the audit team is also asking about encryption for the in-memory representation and logging which processes touch each file, but that feels like a separate conversation.
